Data Processing and Analytics

Real-Time Data Processing

Use our professional expertise in real-time message ingestion, stream, storage, and downstream activation systems to build productive real-time data extracting architecture. Analyze data and make informed decisions as it’s generated.

Data Delivery Optimization

Get a helping hand to transform the old waterfall into an agile data delivery method. We can help you effectively optimize outdated methods, enhance data pipelines, and implement scalable data solutions for faster, more reliable data ingestion.

Data Extraction, Transformation, and Loading

Whether you deal with disparate data sources, handle large volumes of data, or require real-time analytics, we can help you analyze ETL data systems, install new processes, test, extract, and load data coming from various sources into centralized storage.

Data Pipeline Development & Automation

Hire dedicated data specialists who know all about designing, building, and optimizing data workflows that ensure seamless movement, data extracting and storage. Create scalable & automated pipelines with no manual intervention.

Data Analytics and Visualization

Bring in not only technical expertise, but our deep understanding of business processes so that our data engineers can customize interpretation and visualization solutions to your strategies. We can help you uncover trends, make decisions, and communicate insights by integrating data with your company’s tools.

IoT Data Processing

Our dedicated data engineering specialists have extensive experience in developing, managing, and supporting custom-built IoT frameworks and processing systems. Whether you work in retail, logistics, healthcare, manufacturing or any other industry that relies on interconnected devices – we have you covered.

Big Data Technologies

We are using the latest big data tools like Hadoop, Apache Spark, and Apache Kafka to create comprehensive frameworks and transform data into actionable insights. They allow businesses to perform advanced strategies and extract actionable insights to drive more informed decision-making and gain a competitive edge.

Data Engineering Use Cases

Personalized Marketing

Many businesses rely on personalized recommendations to drive user engagement and sales, especially in e-commerce and streaming platforms. Our developers are also proficient in creating systems that collect and process vast amounts of data (browsing history, purchase patterns, preferences) – and apply ML algorithms to boost user experience and increase conversion rates.

Demand Forecasting

Data-driven decision-making is essential for accurate demand forecasting. This is particularly critical for businesses that need to optimize inventory, pricing, and production schedules. Get experienced data analysts proficient in building predictive models, based on data from various sources and factors like historical sales, market trends.

Fault Prediction

In industries like manufacturing, energy, and transportation – predicting equipment failures before they occur always saves costs and reduces downtime. We can help you design systems that pull together data from sensors, maintenance logs, and historical records, effectively detecting patterns that indicate potential failures. By having real-time insights into the current state of machinery, you can avoid costly repairs and delays.

Supply Chain Optimization

Real-time visibility into every step of the supply management process – from sourcing raw materials to delivering products to customers – can help businesses forecast delays, price fluctuations, and demand spikes. By collecting and processing data from suppliers, warehouses, and sales, engineers create systems that enable real-time adjustments in operations and allow for greater cost savings.

Inventory Management

Efficient inventory management is crucial for maintaining the right stock levels and reducing potential overhead costs. Get professional data engineers for hire with experience creating systems to track inventory in real-time, integrating data from point-of-sale systems, supply chain management tools with predictive analytics. This ensures optimal stock levels under reduced shortages and cost optimization.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the key data engineers’s responsibilities?

A data engineer is a key tech specialist when it comes to managing, organizing, and optimizing systems that drive business decisions. The data engineer’s job is to create and maintain data architecture for effective generation, collection, and analysis. Your data engineers are also to be proficient in managing seamless data from various data sources to storage systems and provide ready data access for use by data analysts, data science specialists, and other stakeholders.

What are the main skills of a data engineer?

A data engineer must possess a mix of technical expertise, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills to design and manage data efficiently. Below are the most essential skills to look for:
Programming: C#, Java, Ruby, Bash/Unix Scripting, Scala SQL, Python, R
ETL Processes: tools like Apache NiFi, Talend, Informatica, and Airflow
Big Data Frameworks: Apache Spark, Hadoop, Kafka
Database Management: Relational Databases (SQL), NoSQL Databases
Cloud Computing: AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud
Data Pipeline: tools like Apache Airflow, Luigi, or Prefect
Data Processing: tools like Flink, Spark Streaming, Apache Kafka
Familiarity with Machine Learning and AI.

Why should I hire data engineers with Mobilunity?

Finding the right data specialists may be a challenging task. Hiring with us means you get access to highly skilled data engineers with practical expertise, who successfully solved your type of challenges. You also get cost-effective rates, as we can operate in regions with lower costs of living while maintaining a high level of quality and dedication. Finally, we have flexible engagement models to fit your current needs / global business objectives at their best.

What is the difference between a data engineer and a data analyst?

Basically, a data engineer focuses on building and optimizing the foundation (data frameworks and pipelines), while a data analyst works on top of that foundation to extract actionable insights.

Do I need to hire a data engineer separately for my project?

If your project involves complex data frameworks, real-time processing, large datasets, or requires building infrastructure from scratch, you will have to hire a data engineer separately. This can ensure your data team can focus on data analysis and modeling – rather than spending valuable time and resources on data preparation and system management. If you’re uncertain, tell us about your project and we’ll advise you on the best hiring option or optimal team composition tailored to the unique needs and challenges you are facing.

Should I hire a data engineer full-time or on a part-time basis?

We can help you find and hire data engineers by any engagement model – the final decision depends on your needs. Consider hiring a full-time specialist if you have an ongoing, large-scale project that needs continuous management and infrastructure development. Alternatively, you should go for a part-time data engineer (or consultant) to address a specific area or task in your project, for example setting up systems or migration.

What are the challenges of hiring a data engineer?

Common challenges include finding candidates with the right technical expertise / cultural fit and ensuring they have deep understanding of data, tailored to your specific business needs. Retaining top talents in a highly competitive market is also a challenging thing to do. But we can help you streamline the process of hiring – by sourcing, vetting, and onboarding top-tier specialists for your project.
